molecular replacement can be used for structure determination of proteins with multiple molecules in the unit cell, even when pseudo-crystallography and twinning are present, but the process can be challenging.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to solve the structure of a protein in the face of multiple molecules in the asymmetric unit and pseudo-symmetry, and that the detection of twinning can be difficult when there are multiple molecules per asymmetric unit.
, when faced with multiple molecules, pseudosymmetry, and twinning, one should not give up on molecular replacement too quickly.
, when the structure determination of a protein is difficult, the solution can often be found by looking for the unusual, such as twinning and pseudo-translational symmetries.
